customer_jordan: Hey team — our Feb invoice (INV-2026-02-17) shows ~1.23M tokens but our on-prem meter reports ~905k. This is a large delta and customer is asking for an explanation. We're a VPC/private deployment. Any immediate checks?

sam_support: Sorry about that — we'll dig in. Quick Qs: what agent version are you running, and can you paste the last 200 lines of /var/log/redwood/meter.log? Also, did you see any maintenance/host reboots around Feb 16-18?

customer_jordan: Agent is v1.10.2 on 3 hosts (redwood-agent-01..03). We had a kernel patch on Feb 16 and did a rolling restart. Attached a tiny excerpt from meter.log: 
```
2026-02-17T03:12:04Z INFO buffer: queued 10240 tokens
2026-02-17T03:12:07Z ERROR buffer: flush failed: no space left on device
2026-02-17T03:17:12Z WARNING clock: detected step +301s
2026-02-17T03:17:13Z INFO buffer: recovered, replay scheduled (spool=/var/lib/redwood/spool)
2026-02-17T03:20:59Z INFO replay: uploaded chunk=00023 tokens=324512
```

sam_support: That clock step +301s is a red flag — if agent was buffering offline and the system time jumped forward it can cause the agent to ACK events differently or drop some buffered entries. Can you run the diag tool and upload results? `sudo /opt/redwood/agent/bin/diag --since 2026-02-15 --out /tmp/diag.tar.gz` then `rdw diag-upload /tmp/diag.tar.gz` or paste a presigned link.

customer_jordan: Running diag now. FYI when we checked billing dashboard it showed the spike right at 03:20 UTC and then a flattening. We do have a separate audit log (tenant-side) that shows ~1.24M tokens across app servers for that window. So audit>invoice>meter ordering weird.

elaine_eng: We saw a related pattern in the field with v1.10.2 — when offline buffer hits disk full during a time jump, the spool replay can result in double-uploads or missing ACK bookkeeping depending on S3 retry ordering. There's a fix in v1.10.3 that changes the spool manifest write to be atomic + adds a safe_time_sync flag. If you can, hold on upgrades for a moment but we can provide a hotfix script to reprocess the spool and reconcile counts.

mike_onprem: Confirmed kernel update + chrony restart at 03:15 UTC on all hosts. From syslog on redwood-agent-02: 
```
Feb 17 03:15:52 redwood-agent-02 kernel: systemd: Time has jumped forward by 301.123456s
Feb 17 03:15:53 redwood-agent-02 chronyd[1023]: Selected source 0.debian.pool.ntp.org
Feb 17 03:16:00 redwood-agent-02 rdw-agent[2134]: buffer: write failed: No space left on device
```

sam_support: Thanks — that aligns. Next steps I'd recommend: 1) run the replay dry-run to see how many tokens remain in spool: `sudo /opt/redwood/agent/bin/replay --spool /var/lib/redwood/spool --dry-run --summary` 2) if dry-run shows >0, run `replay --spool ... --to s3://redwood-replay/<tenant>/2026-02-17/` so we can re-ingest missing chunks. Share output.

customer_jordan: Ran dry-run: `dry-run summary: chunks=9 tokens=320420 bytes=12.1MB` Running full replay now...

infra-bot: Deploy monitor: https://console.redwood.example/tenants/12345/replay/1851234567 (auto-created)

customer_jordan: Replay finished: `replayed 9 chunks, 320420 tokens, 0 failures` — after replay our local meter now shows 1,225,430 tokens for the window. That brings us very close to invoice and audit. Will that reconcile billing automatically?

billing_ops: Please DM me the invoice ID and the S3 replay manifest. We usually wait for the replay audit to be ingested into the billing pipeline (1-4 hours). If the replay is accepted, we can open a billing adjustment request and hold the invoice while we confirm. Send the manifest URL and I'll kick off the review.

elaine_eng: To prevent recurrence: 1) upgrade to v1.10.3 (hotfix available), 2) enable `safe_time_sync: true` in /etc/redwood/agent.yml to make the agent resilient to forward clock steps while buffering, 3) ensure spool partition has headroom (recommended 25% free). We can provide a one-line check: `df -h /var/lib/redwood | awk 'NR==2{print $5}'` and alert if >75% used.

mike_onprem: We'll patch to v1.10.3 tonight and enable safe_time_sync. Also added a preemptive cron to run the replay dry-run daily (just in case).

sam_support: Great — thanks for the quick repro and replay. For our records: could you paste the diag-upload link and confirm the customer tenant ID? Also please keep the original spool tarball for 7 days in case we need deep forensic. :thumbsup: 

customer_jordan: diag uploaded -> https://s3.presigned.example/diag-1851234567.tar.gz tenant=acct-12345. We'll keep spool tarball for 7 days. Thanks all.

billing_ops: Got the manifest and invoice ID INV-2026-02-17. I placed a billing hold and opened a ticket BR-9876. Will update once billing pipeline ingests replayed events.

elaine_eng: Filed internal follow-up to backport safe-time logic into older branches for any customers stuck on v1.10.x.

sam_support: Closing loop: root cause = combo of disk-full buffer + forward system time jump during offline buffering which caused partial replay ordering issues. Remediation = replay (done), upgrade to v1.10.3, enable safe_time_sync, ensure spool headroom. Reopen if delta persists.

customer_jordan: Confirmed — delta resolved to within 0.6%, customer satisfied. Thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
